attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter. He states them as his own view, not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The proposition follows the source and keeps the hedge 'the underlying economics suggest'. It is an evaluative judgment about the present, labelled as an observation, with no metric for 'financial sense'.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to turn hedged, evaluative language into a firm claim about profitability. 'Financial sense' has no plain metric (margin, profit or long-run viability), so any score would rest on terms he did not supply.

reviews.rationale: The statement is hedged ('suggest') and evaluative ('any kind of financial sense'), with no metric, set of companies or period. Under policy the plain-reading rule does not apply to hedged language, so the claim cannot be scored. The packet has no evidence items; the one source it considered was marked unused. The case is not broken, just not adjudicable.
